bottlenecks_identified: Synthesis-only task execution accounted for 100% of milestone duration (7 completed tasks totaling 58.2 wall-time minutes), with the longest single experiment ('Qualify installed inference and existing public import contracts') consuming 20.87 minutes (~35.9% of total wall time).
The installed inference and public import contract qualification run executed as an unpartitioned monolithic synthesis pass without intermediate checkpointing or fine-grained intra-phase timeouts.

Recurring orchestration passes—including binding thirteen tasks and sealing deployment protocols (8.15 minutes), mapping newly measured operations to hardware support (8.11 minutes), measuring redirect horizons (8.64 minutes), and reconciling thirteen outcomes (7.02 minutes)—executed full sweeps without incremental caching or memoization on unchanged evidence.

improvements_suggested: Partition prolonged installed inference and public import contract qualification runs into modular sub-checks with early failure detection to prevent unmonitored multi-minute executions.

Introduce incremental receipt caching and evidence memoization for recurring task-binding, hardware-support mapping, redirect horizon measurement, and outcome-reconciliation passes when upstream inputs remain unchanged.
Persist synchronous start, finish, and elapsed execution timestamps directly into experiment JSON receipts to eliminate reliance on disk-mtime fallback reconstruction.
Preserve DualGPURunner boundaries strictly for concurrent multi-model inference pipelines, avoiding unnecessary GPU allocation or runner overhead on CPU-bound synthesis workloads.
Maintain active failure_ledger pre-launch checks to ensure non-viable doomed reruns are aborted in <1s before consuming milestone wall time.

meta_reflection: Milestone 2026.10.741 completed 7 synthesis-only experiments in 58.2 wall-time minutes with zero compute-bound tasks and gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks recorded as null. Observed 0% GPU utilization on GPU 0 was appropriate for CPU synthesis workloads, while GPU 1 ran background inference, and no multi-model tasks were present to require DualGPURunner.
